# mailtrap_sending_domain (Resource)

Manages a Mailtrap sending domain used for email authentication.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "mailtrap_sending_domain" "example" {
  domain_name            = "mail.example.com"
  open_tracking_enabled  = true
  click_tracking_enabled = true
}

# The DNS records to publish for domain verification.
output "dns_records" {
  value = mailtrap_sending_domain.example.dns_records
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain_name` (String) The domain name (e.g. `example.com`). Changing this forces replacement.

### Optional

- `auto_unsubscribe_link_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the automatic unsubscribe link is enabled.
- `click_tracking_enabled` (Boolean) Whether click tracking is enabled.
- `open_tracking_enabled` (Boolean) Whether open tracking is enabled.

### Read-Only

- `compliance_status` (String) Compliance review status of the domain.
- `demo` (Boolean) Whether this is a demo domain.
- `dns_records` (Attributes List) DNS records to publish to authenticate the domain. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dns_records))
- `dns_verified` (Boolean) Whether the domain's DNS records have been verified.
- `id` (Number) Numeric identifier of the sending domain.

<a id="nestedatt--dns_records"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dns_records`

Read-Only:

- `domain` (String)
- `key` (String)
- `name` (String)
- `status` (String)
- `type` (String)
- `value` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a sending domain by its numeric ID.
terraform import mailtrap_sending_domain.example 12345
```
